title: Terraform drift detection and safe provider-upgrade harness for networking stacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Multiple incidents and ongoing toil from small networking changes have exposed drift between declared Terraform state and cloud resources. Additionally, upgrading the AWS provider and other providers during prior attempts caused subtle resource replacements and prolonged outage windows for staging environments. This ticket scopes a durable, opinionated drift-detection and safe-upgrade harness that reduces blast radius for provider upgrades and module interface changes, and provides automated remediation guardrails for networking stacks.

Goals:
- Detect drift continuously for critical networking modules (VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT, EIPs).
- Block accidental destructive provider upgrades via CI guard rails and compatibility checks.
- Provide a staged, automated migration path for safe provider upgrades and breaking module changes (canary workspace, plan review, automated rollback).
- Decouple module variable surfaces to allow additive changes without forcing wide rollouts.

Out of scope: full org-wide provider upgrades for non-networking modules (will be handled in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Continuous drift-check job runs every 6 hours and posts a summary to #infra-alerts with links to failing plans
CI pipelines fail provider-upgrade merge when any change replaces or recreates networking resources without an approved migration plan
A canary workspace exists for networking changes that applies to a single-region small VPC and runs smoke tests before wider rollout
Documentation and runbook for emergency manual rollback and state restore published in Confluence
Module interfaces updated to maintain backward-compatible defaults; one compatibility shim implemented and tested
risks: False positives from drift checks causing noise and alert fatigue
Complex provider upgrade interactions (provider vX -> vY) that require manual TF state manipulation
CI job runtime and API rate limits when planning at org scale
rollout_plan: 1) Implement drift-check GitHub Action: terraform init + terraform plan against remote state, save plan JSON and diff summary
2) Target networking modules first: create dedicated 'networking-drifts' job that runs every 6h and after every PR merge
3) Introduce provider compatibility matrix file in infra repo mapping module versions to pinned provider versions
4) Add CI gate: provider-version-change detection fails merge and requires a manual 'upgrade plan' approval ticket
5) Create canary workspace and terraform workspace automation to apply canary changes automatically during off-hours with automated smoke tests
6) Run provider upgrade in canary, validate smoke tests, escalate to staged rollout (two-region apply), then full rollout
7) Post-mortem and tidy-up: remove compatibility shims no earlier than 30 days after successful staged rollout
implementation_notes: Use terraform 1.6+ plan JSON outputs to parse diffs; combine with a lightweight parser (Python) to detect resource replacements
Store drift plan artifacts in S3 with object lifecycle; index by module and workspace for quick lookup
Prefer non-disruptive tfstate transforms; avoid force-replace unless documented in migration plan
Lock provider versions in module root with a pinned 'provider-lock.hcl' file and surface an automated update PR generator
Consider using remote state 'read-only' role for CI drift checks to avoid accidental applies from CI runners
testing_notes: Smoke tests: pod-to-pod connectivity across subnets, NAT egress test, route propagation verification
Introduce a test harness that can spin up a small VPC in the 'canary' account and run the full apply+smoke test in <30 minutes
Manual verification steps documented for initial run: sanity checklist for network ACLs, route tables, and IGW attachments
comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after post-incident review (networking drift incident 2026-02-09). Initial scope and goals added.

2026-02-18 Diego Alvarez: Investigated prior provider-upgrade attempt. Found that provider v5.12 -> v6.0 changed default lifecycle behavior for aws_eip causing replacements. Added compatibility shim idea to implementation notes.
2026-02-25 Priya Menon (Infra QA): PoC drift-check action merged to feature branch; runs against staging workspace and reports plan artifacts to S3. Smoke tests still flaky due to timing - iterating.

2026-03-02 Liam O'Connor (SRE): Reviewed rollout_plan. Suggested adding a 'dry-apply' phase where we run terraform apply with a retained 'oplog' for easy rollback. Also suggested scheduled maintenance window for canary applies.

2026-03-06 Diego Alvarez: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/12345 implementing drift-check action and provider-change detector. Added unit tests for plan-parser. CI passing on feature branch.

2026-03-10 Security Team (notes): Security review required for canary automation credentials. Recommending using short-lived STS role with MFA enforced for manual approvals. Marking ticket for security sign-off before canary run.
